effects: They inherit the climate, resource and institutional effects of present decisions; the UN Declaration on Future Generations recognises that present 'decisions, actions and inactions' have 'an intergenerational multiplier effect'.
voice_today: Wales's Well-being of Future Generations Act 2015 and its Commissioner; the UN Declaration on Future Generations (September 2024); none in AI governance.

effects: UNICEF's 2025 guidance names AI companions used by children, child labour in AI supply chains, datasets contaminated with harmful content, AI-generated child sexual abuse material and environmental impacts that 'particularly impact children'.
voice_today: UNICEF and the Convention on the Rights of the Child; national child-safety regulators; children's commissioners in some countries.

effects: Bear the land, water, energy and mineral demands of compute; permacomputing and degrowth sources point to hyperscale data centres for generative AI.
voice_today: Rights-of-nature law: Ecuador's 2008 constitution; New Zealand's Te Awa Tupua Act 2017 made the Whanganui River a legal person with human guardians. None reaches AI compute today.

effects: Anthropic's own data show Claude use 'strongly correlates with income': Indonesia at 0.36x, India at 0.27x and Nigeria at 0.2x expected use, while Israel is at 7x.
voice_today: ITU and UN development bodies; the Global Digital Compact (2024); no seat in any lab's governance.

effects: 2.2 billion people were offline in 2025, 96% of them in low- and middle-income countries; they bear AI's effects on labour markets, prices and public services without access to its benefits.
voice_today: ITU (universal connectivity mandate); national universal-service regulators.

group: Non-English speakers and speakers of low-resource languages
effects: Large language models are weaker in languages with less digitised text (the 'resourcedness gap'), and are used for content moderation, hiring and public-benefits decisions in those languages.
voice_today: Language communities and research collectives (e.g. Masakhane, Te Hiku Media); no institution with a lever on developers.

effects: TIME found Kenyan labellers paid about $1.32-2 per hour to label graphic text for a ChatGPT safety filter; all four interviewed described being 'mentally scarred'.
voice_today: Unions forming in Nairobi (content moderators' union, 2023); Kenyan courts; no AI-governance seat.

group: Authors and creators whose work trained models (living)
effects: Their books and works were copied into training corpora; authors sued Anthropic as a class and settled (Bartz).
voice_today: Courts and class actions; publishers' and authors' associations.

group: Authors and creators whose work trained models (dead) and their estates
effects: Their works are in corpora too; public-domain works have no living claimant, and estates can sue only while copyright lasts.
voice_today: Estates and literary executors while copyright subsists; no one after it lapses.

effects: In South Memphis, xAI ran dozens of gas turbines without air permits to power its Colossus data centres; Reuters reported in 2026 the pollution hits Black communities hardest.
voice_today: Local air and water regulators, county boards, civil-rights litigants (NAACP, SELC); no seat in lab governance.

group: Communities near mines for chips and battery minerals
effects: Amnesty and Afrewatch documented children as young as seven mining cobalt in the DRC, at least 80 artisanal miners killed underground in 15 months, and electronics brands unable to trace their cobalt.
voice_today: OECD due-diligence guidance; supply-chain laws in some jurisdictions; NGOs; no lever on AI developers.

effects: PJM's market monitor found data-centre load the 'primary reason' capacity costs rose by $7.3 billion (82%) in the 2025 auction, costs passed through to consumers' bills.
voice_today: State utility commissions, consumer advocates and PJM's independent market monitor.

effects: The ILO estimates one in four workers globally is in an occupation with some generative-AI exposure; 3.3% in the highest category, with women more exposed (4.7% vs 2.4%).
voice_today: Trade unions, labour ministries, the ILO; collective bargaining where it exists.

effects: The Dutch tax authority's risk-profiling algorithm used nationality as a risk factor for childcare-benefit fraud, which Amnesty found resulted in discrimination and racial profiling.
voice_today: Data-protection authorities, courts, the EU AI Act's high-risk regime and the GDPR's rules on automated decisions.

effects: The UN Special Rapporteur's 2021-22 thematic report examined how AI can discriminate against disabled people in employment, benefits and services, as well as its potential benefits.
voice_today: UN Special Rapporteur on the rights of persons with disabilities; the CRPD; disabled people's organisations (e.g. European Disability Forum).

effects: Indigenous data and knowledge are taken into open datasets without consent; GIDA states that emphasis on data sharing 'creates a tension' with Indigenous control of their own data.
voice_today: Indigenous governance bodies and GIDA's CARE principles; UNDRIP; community licences such as Te Hiku Media's.

effects: Anthropic reported a criminal who used Claude Code to attack at least 17 organisations, including healthcare, emergency services and religious institutions, with ransom demands sometimes above $500,000.
voice_today: Law enforcement and national cyber agencies; victims' own security teams; no standing against the developer.

effects: WHO's policy brief finds AI in health can 'exacerbate or introduce new forms of ageism' where older people are under-represented in data and design.
voice_today: WHO; the UN Independent Expert on older persons; national age-discrimination law.

effects: Prisoners in two Finnish prisons labelled training data for an AI startup, paid through the prison agency; researchers questioned whether it was training or 'really old forms of labor exploitation'.
voice_today: Prison oversight bodies and courts; no labour representation in AI supply chains.

group: Migrants and people on the move
effects: Molnar's EDRi report, from over 40 conversations with refugees and people on the move, found border AI and automated immigration decisions deployed with little regulation, treating them as 'guinea pigs'.
voice_today: UN Special Rapporteur on racism (2020 report on digital border technologies); refugee-rights NGOs; the EU AI Act's migration provisions.
